solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Loud decoration missing central point

indicators.note: missing central means the letter taken away is the one at the very middle of the decoration word

parts.note: a garnish is a decoration added to a dish
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A garish ornament that lacks a focal point in its middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing central' removes the middle letter of GARNISH, which is N, a compass 'point' (north).
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: loud colours or clothes are gaudy and showy.

clue.text: Picture showing a nice rug damaged

indicators.note: damaged means the letters are broken up and put together differently

explanation.surface: A painting showing a rug that is worn and spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges A NICE RUG.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Guernica is Picasso's famous 1937 painting of the bombing of a Basque town.

clue.text: Lure in a 50s dandy after engineers had another shot

indicators.note: after means the following letters come behind the engineers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps

indicators.note: in means the lure word goes inside the other letters

parts.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth who dressed in Edwardian-style clothes
to tempt is to lure

explanation.surface: Engineers try again to draw a 1950s Teddy boy in.
explanation.walkthrough: A Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth who wore Edwardian-style suits; 'in' and 'after' arrange the pieces, and the Royal Engineers come first.
explanation.definitionFit: A paraphrase: to have another go at something is to try it again.

clue.text: Picture game

definitions.meaning: a card game in which players call out when two matching cards appear

explanation.surface: A game played with pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is a casual photo, and also a simple card game for matching pairs.

clue.text: Easily able to accommodate pushing back limits on debts

indicators.note: pushing back means the limits word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: caps are upper limits, as on spending
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: Someone can comfortably handle having the ceilings on their borrowing delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pushing back' looks like postponing, but it turns the limits word round to SPAC. An IOU is a signed note saying 'I owe you'.
explanation.definitionFit: A roomy place has plenty of space, so it can take in a lot without strain.

clue.text: Being short of breath inspires one picture

indicators.note: inspires, literally breathes in, means the first word takes the one letter inside it

parts.note: panting means gasping, being short of breath
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A breathless person is moved to create a work of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspires' (breathes in) puts I inside PANTING, which suits the breathless picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: an oil or watercolour artwork is a picture.

clue.text: Complaints about picture being mine, mine, mine!

indicators.note: about means the complaints word goes round the film

parts.note: colds are minor illnesses, or complaints
Alfie is a 1966 film starring Michael Caine

explanation.surface: Someone moans about a painting and greedily insists it all belongs to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine, mine, mine!' sounds like a possessive cry, but it means several pits. 'about' wraps the complaints round the 1966 Michael Caine film.
explanation.definitionFit: Coalfields are regions containing many coal mines.

clue.text: Jedi now a bit cut off, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly means the letters come out in an unexpected new order
cut off means the last letter of bit is chopped away

explanation.surface: A Jedi is now, unexpectedly, slightly separated from the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut off' drops the T from BIT to leave BI, and 'surprisingly' rearranges NOW A BI.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Obi-Wan Kenobi is the Jedi Master in the Star Wars films.

clue.text: After climb, old queen is a burnt colour

indicators.note: after a climb means the letters read upwards in this down clue, so they run backwards

parts.note: Anne was Queen of Great Britain in the early 18th century

explanation.surface: After an ascent, a former queen goes red from the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'After climb' means the letters read upwards. Burnt sienna is the pigment's usual full name, so 'burnt' belongs with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnt sienna is a reddish-brown earth pigment used by painters.

clue.text: Award lunch for one entertaining director

indicators.note: entertaining means the meal word holds the director letter, as a host holds a guest

parts.note: lunch is one example of a meal

explanation.surface: A prize of lunch given to someone hosting a film director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts D inside MEAL. 'for one' marks lunch as just one example of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a medal is a decoration awarded for achievement or bravery.

clue.text: Compelled to return in the morning with low-grade beans

indicators.note: to return means the word for compelled is read backwards

parts.note: made someone do something means compelled them
AM, ante meridiem, marks a morning time
E is a low grade in exams

explanation.surface: Someone forced to come back each morning to eat poor-quality beans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reverses MADE to give EDAM, followed by AM and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Edamame are young green soya beans served in the pod, popular in Japanese cooking.

clue.text: Picture international soldier in shock

indicators.note: in means the soldier is put inside the shock word

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it, like a mane
GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: Think of a foreign soldier suffering from shell shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' looks like the trauma sense but means a mass of hair; 'in' puts the soldier inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as verbs: to picture something is to form a mental image of it.

clue.text: Catches alien between poles

indicators.note: between means the alien letters sit inside the two poles

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles
ET is the film alien, the Extra-Terrestrial

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial is caught somewhere between the North and South Poles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' places ET between N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to net something is to catch it, as a fisherman or a goal scorer does.

clue.text: Brewing of tea needs picture

indicators.note: brewing means the letters are stirred up and worked into something new

explanation.surface: Making tea properly calls for a picture of the process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brewing' rearranges OF TEA NEEDS. 'of' is part of the letters, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: East of Eden is a 1955 film starring James Dean, and 'picture' is a common word for a film.

clue.text: Dreadful picture taken by journalist in Delaware shows old problem

indicators.note: in means all of this sits inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: DE is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Delaware

indicators.note: taken by means the journalist letters take in the jumbled word

parts.note: ED is an editor, a journalist

indicators.note: dreadful means the letters are badly messed up into a new order

explanation.surface: An awful photo taken by a reporter in Delaware reveals a long-standing issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' rearranges the word picture into CREPITU; 'taken by' and 'in' then wrap the journalist and the state round it in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepitude is the frailty and weakness that comes with old age, a problem of being old.

clue.text: Original note omitted from strait- laced prayer-book

parts.note: prim means prudish and strait-laced

indicators.note: omitted from means the note letter is left out of the words that follow

parts.note: an ordinal is a service book of church rites

explanation.surface: A first music note left out of an old-fashioned book of prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omitted from' takes N (note) out of PRIM + ORDINAL. 'note' suggests a musical letter, but it is N.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something primordial existed from the beginning of time, so it is the earliest, first of its kind.

clue.text: One taking picture of artist arrived earlier

indicators.note: earlier means the arrived word goes before the artist

parts.note: came means arrived
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Someone photographing a painter who turned up ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earlier' moves the arrival in front of the artist, reversing the order the clue gives them.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a camera is the device that takes a photograph.

clue.text: Popular bishop possibly reported as enjoying calm

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: reported means the word is given by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a bishop is one example of a chess piece

explanation.surface: A well-liked bishop is said to lead a tranquil life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' turns PIECE into its sound-alike PEACE. 'possibly' marks the bishop as just one example of a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to be in peace is to be untroubled and tranquil.

clue.text: Traces letters about unpleasant people returning

indicators.note: about means the letters word wraps round the others

parts.note: vees are letter V's

indicators.note: returning means the word for the unpleasant people is read backwards

parts.note: gits is British slang for unpleasant or contemptible people

explanation.surface: Following the trail of letters about nasty people who come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Git' is British slang for a contemptible person; 'letters' looks like correspondence but means letters of the alphabet spelt out, here two vees; 'returning' turns the slang word round to STIG and 'about' wraps the vees round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: vestiges are remaining signs or remnants of something that has otherwise gone.

clue.text: Surprised the beginning came first

parts.note: the start is the beginning
led means came first, as in a race

explanation.surface: Amazed that the opening arrived ahead of everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: someone surprised by something sudden is startled or alarmed.

clue.text: Out in poker game, politician essentially clean

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the poker word

parts.note: stud is a form of poker
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: essentially means the core, central letter of the word clean is taken

explanation.surface: A clean-living politician gets knocked out of a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes the middle letter of 'clean', and 'in' puts it with the politician inside the poker game. In cricket a batsman is stumped when the keeper breaks the wicket with him out of his ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumped is a way of being dismissed in cricket, so it is a kind of 'out'.

clue.text: Extremely strange wood destined to be cut down

indicators.note: cut down means the outer parts of the words are trimmed away, leaving a run of letters inside

explanation.surface: Very oddly, timber that is fated to be felled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' trims the phrase 'wood destined' down to the run of letters inside it. The forestry picture makes 'cut down' look like felling.
explanation.definitionFit: A superlative: most peculiar means extremely strange.

clue.text: University's head of drama the original bad actor

indicators.note: head of means just the opening letter of drama is used

parts.note: ur- is a prefix meaning original or earliest, as in Urtext
a ham is an overacting, bad actor

explanation.surface: A university's drama head was the first terrible performer.
explanation.walkthrough: D, the 'head of drama', is followed by UR and HAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Durham University is a long-established university in north-east England.

clue.text: Problems getting horse aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard means the horse goes inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: Trouble arises getting a horse onto a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aboard' is a container signal here: the horse goes between the steamship letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a snag is a hitch or unexpected difficulty.

clue.text: Get picture below spectator accommodation

parts.note: under means below
a stand at a sports ground is where spectators sit

explanation.surface: Taking a photograph from beneath the grandstand at a sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to 'get the picture' is to grasp or comprehend what is meant.

clue.text: Bank's relationship to the monarch

parts.note: a tie is a bond or relationship
R stands for Rex or Regina, the monarch

explanation.surface: A financial institution's links with the Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests a financial institution, but it means a row or tier, as of seats or oars.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bank is a row or level, like a tier of seats or oars.

clue.text: Picture Johnson arguing with Saudi leaders

indicators.note: leaders means the first letter of each of the preceding words is taken

explanation.surface: A photo of Boris Johnson in dispute with Saudi rulers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes the first letters of Johnson, arguing, with, Saudi.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Jaws is Steven Spielberg's 1975 shark film, and 'picture' means a film.

clue.text: Clearing his throat, Hemming's usual partner welcomes Kelvin

indicators.note: welcomes means the first word takes the kelvin letter in

parts.note: people dithering are said to be hemming and hawing, so hawing goes with hemming
K is the symbol for kelvin, the unit of temperature

explanation.surface: A man called Hemming coughs while his regular partner receives someone named Kelvin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomes' puts K inside HAWING. 'Hemming' looks like a surname, but it comes from the phrase 'hemming and hawing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to hawk is to clear the throat noisily, so this is the -ing form.

clue.text: See 7
Allow a pair of books to be removed step by step

indicators.note: to be removed means the books letters are taken out

parts.note: to grant is to allow
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books
dual means made of a pair, twofold

explanation.surface: Permission to take away two books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be removed' takes the New Testament out of the allow word, leaving GRA. 'a pair of books' looks like one unit but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something that proceeds by degrees happens gradually, a little at a time.

clue.text: Picture of animal so moving

indicators.note: moving means the letters are shifted around into a new order

explanation.surface: A painting of a creature that is so touching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges ANIMAL SO. It looks like 'emotionally touching' but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Leonardo's Mona Lisa is perhaps the most famous painting in the world.

clue.text: City where large number died

parts.note: OS means outsize, extra large in clothing
ten is a number
D is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A place where many people lost their lives.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a crossword convention for large.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Ostend is a port city on the Belgian coast.
